size.notes: FishBase gives a 109 cm TL maximum (12.5 kg by this LWR, above the world record); the Florida Museum's longest recorded fish is 87 cm. lengthCm.max set to 100 cm, where the LWR meets the record.

migration.notes: Adults usually hold in deeper water and move into the shallows at night and in the breeding season (Florida Museum).

markings.notes: round to oval black spot; in mature males ringed orange-yellow (#e8a23a); faint or absent in mature females, present in all juveniles
yellow-brown head with darker horizontal bars

pattern.fins: very long, low dorsal fin (42-53 rays) running most of the back; paired and anal fins vivid green; rounded tail light olive with irregular dark vertical bars

variants.spawning_male: fins bright green and the tail-spot ring a more intense orange
variants.juvenile: black tail spot in both sexes; young travel in a tight swarm guarded by the male

pattern.source: Florida Museum of Natural History bowfin profile; FishBase short description; South Carolina DNR

regulations.notes: Nongame fish: no bag or length limit.

economy.notes: Edible but little valued; mercury builds up in the flesh, and badly cooked flesh is said to ball up in the mouth ('cottonfish').

facts: Bowfin breathe air through their gas bladder: hardly at all at 4-10 C, most of all between about 18 and 30 C.
The male builds the nest, then guards the eggs and a tight swarm of young for months.
It is the lone surviving species of its family, a true 'living fossil'.

research.task: Catch one on a spinnerbait in weedy water
Observe a male guarding his swarm of young

ledger.wrenNote: Bowfin save the worst for the boat. Ease the drag a touch before he gets there, net him, don't lift him, and keep your fingers out of that mouth.
